text:
deploy-bot: Started rollout: web-inference v2.9.1 -> 20% traffic across eu-west / us-central. rollout_id=rl-20240430-09

maya: seeing a p95 jump on the served-text route right after the shift. p95 ~ 780ms -> 1.8s. dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/served-text?s=now-15m :eyes:

liam: agh. also a small uptick in 429s on the quota proxy for the same route. sampling trace attached (short):
```
trace: service=quota-proxy latency=12ms -> backend=embed-cache p95=1.6s
log: "quota_proxy: rate-limit=exceeded for client_id=svc-frontend-1"
```

sre-oncall: thanks — grabbing the full traces. tagging this as SLO-early-warning. what's the error-budget burn rate last 1h?

maya: error budget burn ~ 7% in last hour for served-text p95 SLO. overall 30d budget still healthy.

ops-bot: Alert: 429 spike detected on route=served-text. threshold=0.5% current=1.7% window=5m. alert_id=A-7592

nate: I've got a quick hypothesis: recent client-side batching change in v2.9.1 increases concurrency to quota-proxy; combined with a small eviction storm on the local KV cache, tail latency amplifies.

liam: can we quickly check node-level qps and connection counts? `kubectl top pods -l app=web-inference` and `ss -ntp | grep quota-proxy`

maya: running checks now — one pod in eu-west-1 showing CPU spike and connection backlog. pod/web-inference-7f4c9   CPU 92%   connections ~ 800 (normal ~ 120)

sre-oncall: ok let's do a targeted rollback for the eu-west traffic slice while we triage. options: 1) pause rollout (deploy-bot rollback 10% -> 0), 2) pin eu-west routing to v2.8.0, 3) scale quota-proxy horizontally. Preference is to stop the blast radius quickly.

nate: I can scale quota-proxy now but that won't address the KV eviction behavior. I'd vote: pin eu-west to v2.8.0 and pause the rollout. then we can run a replicable load test against v2.9.1 with verbose tracing.

liam: +1 pin. how do we pin in the router? `infractl route set web-inference --region eu-west --version v2.8.0`

maya: executing pin now. output:
```
$ infractl route set web-inference --region eu-west --version v2.8.0
Routing update queued: change_id=chg-9923 target=eu-west
Applied to 4 routers, draining v2.9.1 connections
```

deploy-bot: Rollout paused by maya. rollout_id=rl-20240430-09 status=paused traffic=v2.9.1@20% -> eu-west pinned to v2.8.0. Audit: maya

ops-bot: Incident note: pinned routing for eu-west; started an autoscale action for quota-proxy +2 replicas.

sre-oncall: good. please collect a heap/profile from the offending pod and dump KV-cache metrics (hit_rate, evictions/sec) — that will confirm the eviction storm hypothesis.

nate: grabbing pod heap and metrics now. `kubectl exec -it pod/web-inference-7f4c9 -- curl localhost:9090/metrics | grep kv_cache`

maya: quick follow-up — can we add a short dashboard panel to show `client_batch_size` distribution for served-text? v2.9.1 changed batching defaults. if client-side batches doubled, that explains the concurrency bump.

liam: added a temp panel on the dashboard for `client_batch_size` and grouped by version. link: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/served-text?view=batch-dist

nate: metrics show client_batch_size median 3 -> 6 for v2.9.1, and kv_cache.evictions/sec spiked from 2 -> 57 during the first 3 minutes of rollout. that lines up.

sre-oncall: good catch. Root cause likely interactive: larger batches -> more concurrent KV working set -> evictions -> higher tail latency -> client retries -> 429s. Action items: revert batching change in next patch or tune client to cap batch size, add a graceful backoff in quota-proxy, and create a canary test that simulates client batch distributions.

maya: logging action items to the release ticket and will reopen the rollout when we have patch v2.9.2 and a canary run with controlled batch sizes.

liam: adding a postmortem note: include timeline, KV metrics, sample traces and the infractl pin command used.

deploy-bot: Rollout resume blocked until status=approved and patch release v2.9.2 is merged. Audit log created.

sre-oncall: closing this thread for now — if anyone sees any more 429s after the pin, ping here and we'll escalate. thanks all :thumbsup:
